22.t: Working with data: the cardiac cycle
q: One beat lasts 0.8 s, so 60 / 0.8 = 75 beats per minute.
Identify the time when the aortic (semilunar) valve opens. Explain.
At about 0.12–0.15 s, when ventricular pressure rises above aortic pressure.
Identify the time when the atrioventricular valve closes. Explain.
At about 0.05 s, when ventricular pressure rises above atrial pressure, pushing the valve shut.
Explain why aortic pressure never falls below about 80 mmHg, while ventricular pressure falls almost to zero.
The semilunar valve closes, so blood cannot flow back, and the elastic wall of the aorta recoils, keeping pressure up while blood flows on.
In hard exercise one beat lasts 0.4 s. Suggest which phase is shortened most and one effect.
Diastole (relaxation and filling) is shortened most; there is less time for the ventricles to fill and for blood to flow through the coronary arteries.
